text:
⛔️ "Stop spreading democracy here. Communicate with people in their language." – That's what the CEO of a defence tech company told me after my first few days there.

I'd taken a parallel position at a hierarchical, command-driven organization. At the same time, I was working at Speed and Function, one of the most self-organizing companies I've experienced with open channels, horizontal decisions, individual ownership at every level.

The gap between these two cultures skips entire developmental stages. And I was living in both simultaneously.

In Spiral Dynamics, organizations evolve through distinct stages:
🔴 Red is built on power: one leader commands, others obey, loyalty is personal, and control flows through fear and reward. 
🩵 Teal operates on wholeness: authority is distributed, people self-manage, and the organization adapts like a living system. 

You can't bridge these stages by simply switching your behavior. They run on fundamentally different assumptions about what makes people act.

The CEO's advice made sense. In his world, directive leadership was the operating model. Most of the team weren't the autonomous tech people. They were factory and office workers operating within an authority-driven worldview – a different stage that required a matching approach.

So I tried. I started behaving directively. Within days, it caused a conflict with one employee. She escalated to the CEO. He managed to resolve her complaint, but the relationship between her and me was permanently destroyed.

Here's the paradox: the CEO was building a hierarchical company where directive management was the norm. He could demand direct execution of his orders. But he couldn't transfer that authority to me. Because in a Red organization, authority isn't positional – it's personal. It lives in the relationship between the leader and each person. No relationship, no authority.

My initial assumption was that different cultures simply require different leadership styles. Match the style to the stage, and you're fine. But I was wrong.

I learned that relationships between people matter in every system. In a self-organizing company like Speed and Function, investing in relationships multiplies capability across the whole system. In a hierarchical company, skipping that investment traps you in permanent micromanagement.

The skill that matters most – building real relationships – is the same everywhere. The consequences of ignoring it just look different.

And what about your world? Which Spiral Dynamics stage does your organization run on?

🔴 Red – power, loyalty, one leader decides 
🔵 Blue – rules, hierarchy, process above all 
🟠 Orange – results, competition, meritocracy 
🟢 Green – consensus, equality, shared values 
🟡 Yellow – systems thinking, flexibility, autonomy 
🩵 Teal – wholeness, self-management, evolutionary purpose

Just drop your color in the comments, please.
